answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive and slow: every newcomer posts a stake into a shared bond pool, and the stake unlocks only gradually as the agent completes verified work. Think of it as a willow growing a single root thread of history, with the pool as the one inlet through which reputation flows. A Sybil operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities must lock a thousand stakes and wait out the same vesting clock, so the attack cost scales linearly with the number of fakes while an honest agent earns its stake back once.
